definition: In this historical usage, psychological aesthetics refers to the aspect of aesthetics concerned with the senses and feelings involved in beauty. In the source, it includes especially sight and hearing, and to a lesser extent smell, as giving relatively pure pleasures through colour, form, and clear, simple sounds.
